donor.note: Same publisher's Windows port of the same engine build, already installable (32/33 sites, confidence 1.0, resolved directly from this binary's own native namespace-qualified symbols). Used here as the match source instead of a cross-platform donor.

matcher_calibration.note: The already-published calibration in data/adjudication/METHOD.md section 1 (run v1 sourced from binary 22 into binary 19, a fully-named Mac donor) applies directly here, since the source side and matching technique are identical -- only the destination differs. margin 0.15-0.30 -> ~85-91% loose agreement, margin 0.30+ -> ~89% loose agreement, margin 0.000 -> ~9-10% agreement (untrustworthy). A fresh self-calibration against binary 23's own native names was attempted but is not viable: only 128 of 26965 functions carry name_origin='namespace' (a real symbol), and none are game-engine classes -- they are MSVC STL/MFC/ATL/Concurrency-Runtime symbols pulled in from the runtime library, not NWScript VM code. binary 23 has no locally-verifiable ground truth of its own for the classes this table needs.

accept_rule: Same as METHOD.md: accept requires at least two independent signals, at least one of which is not run v1 (shape/size/n_blocks/n_callees comparison against the known-good binary 22 site, or a distinguishing instruction pattern read directly from the binary). A calibrated-trustworthy match margin alone is not sufficient.
counts_note: 7 of the 12 required VM/stack sites accepted. The remaining 5 required sites (StackPopInteger, StackPushInteger, StackPopFloat, StackPopObject, StackPushObject) are a genuine degenerate cluster in this binary: 12 consecutive 28-40-byte one-block one-callee thunks at 0x6fd980-0x6fdb10, structurally near-identical, that run v1 collapsed onto the same destination address for every one of the 5 gog_aspyr sources. This is NOT identical-code-folding -- direct disassembly confirms all 12 thunks are genuinely distinct functions calling 12 distinct callees (0x703810, 0x702b60, 0x702be0, 0x702c30, 0x702cb0, 0x702d00, 0x702d70, 0x702dd0, 0x702e60, 0x702f20, 0x702fe0, 0x703070) -- but distinguishing WHICH thunk is which requires either a discriminating instruction pattern inside each callee (attempted for one callee, 0x703810: it dispatches through a vtable-shaped member-function-pointer call with no literal type-code immediate anywhere in the first 0x40 bytes, unlike METHOD.md's AddToTopOfStack discriminator on the Linux build) or exhaustive positional TU-layout matching against binary 22's declaration order, which this pass did not complete to accept-grade confidence. Note that StackPopString/StackPushString, structurally identical in shape to the collapsed members, were NOT part of the collapse -- run v1 placed them at their own distinct addresses, which is itself evidence the matcher's underlying features distinguish them even though a from-scratch disassembly reading does not obviously show why. installable stays false until the remaining 5 are done; see the unresolved sites' method_detail below for exactly what would settle it.

Direct disassembly of 0x6FD980-0x6FDB10 shows 12 genuinely distinct thunks (not identical-code-folded), but none carries a discriminating signal this pass could extract in the time available -- disassembling one candidate callee (0x703810) found a vtable-dispatch pattern with no literal type-code immediate, unlike the AddToTopOfStack discriminator METHOD.md found on the Linux build. Rejected as unresolved rather than guessed.
